Is my small business exempt from the Israeli website accessibility regulations?
I need a self-hosted accessibility menu instead of paying for AccessiBe on my Israeli site

lessons: First review of this skill since it was contributed. The legal floor was wrong: it presented WCAG 2.1 AA as equal to ת"י 5568, which is WCAG 2.0-based (May 2021 Part 1). Corrected, with 2.1/2.2 framed as a stricter target.

The statement contents were misaligned with תקנה 35ה: the one item that applies to everyone (a contact route for reporting a missing adaptation) was missing, while the coordinator was presented as universal though the law requires one only from 25 employees (s.19מב).

Widget-equals-compliance framing removed from the body, both descriptions and the statement template, which had the site assert full WCAG 2.1 AA conformance unconditionally. Template now defaults to partial conformance with placeholders (Tier C safe harbour) and cites the FTC accessiBe order.

Five code defects found by review and two more by the arithmetic pass: persist-before-restore wiped saved settings on every load; the RTL thumb had no physical anchor; the on-offset was 21px where 44-18-3=23; textLarge/textSmall could both be set; var(--red) was undefined so focus outlines silently vanished; the toggle was sized in rem while the widget itself changes the root font size; and contrast mode blacked out the widget's own switches.
Lesson for any widget skill: a feature that changes the root font size cannot size its own controls in rem, and a mode that recolours everything must exempt the control surface that operates it.

Overlap with israeli-accessibility-compliance measured 0.757 before the description was narrowed. The boundary now names that slug for exemptions, enforcement and full-site audits, and overlap fell below the warn threshold.

Deferred over the batch discretionary cap: a worked axe/keyboard/screen-reader verification walkthrough; i18n of the panel labels (currently Hebrew only); prefers-contrast and forced-colors handling; background-image and box-shadow survival in contrast mode; the 3 cosmetic round-2 nits were fixed rather than deferred.

Not verified this cycle: whether an edition of ת"י 5568 later than May 2021 adopts WCAG 2.1 (sii.org.il was not reachable for a paid standard). Re-check next cycle before changing the WCAG-version statement.

Follow-up 1.1.1: the complex-:not() fix had been applied to the contrast rule only, while the readable-font rule kept :not(svg *). A whole-rule invalidation makes a mode fail silently, so when fixing this class of defect, grep every rule in the file rather than the one the reviewer named.

Pre-existing, logged not fixed: the readable-font rule excludes the <code> and <pre> ELEMENTS but not their descendants, so a highlighted block (Prism/Shiki/highlight.js wraps tokens in spans) renders mixed, Arial tokens against monospace runs. True in 1.0.3 and every version since. Fix needs a descendant-aware exclusion, which cannot use a complex :not() argument, so it wants a different approach (e.g. scoping the rule to a content root).

Specificity lesson from the 1.1.1 repair loop, three rounds burnt: excluding an element from an inherited-property rule never protects it, because the ancestor still matched and the value inherits down. :not(svg *) was cosmetic in every version. `inherit` and `revert` both resolve back to the poisoned ancestor value; only `initial` or an explicit stack escapes, and a repeated class adds one class per occurrence, not one per repetition. When a guard needs this much cleverness, state the tradeoff in a comment instead.
